2. Short facts involved in this case is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted title suit No. 86 of 1991 on 14-1-1991 for permanent injunction against the defendant-opposite parties in the court of Assistant Judge, Bagerhat, alleging, inter alia, that the suit property measuring 5-89 acres of land of S. A. Khatian Nos. 202, 378, 145, 424, 542, 593 of Kalidia Mouza No. 81 and of S. A. Khatian Nos. 64, 148 of Mouza Chargram No. 79 and of S. A. Khatian Nos. 109, 207 of Mouza Alukdia No. 80 which originally belonged to Nagendra Nath Biswas, Khagendra Nath Biswas, Sudhir Chandra Biswas, Monoranjan Biswas and lndumati were exchanged with the 41/4th of the Indian Properties of one Kalimuddin as per Exchange-Agreement between the parties on 16-7-1964. Kalimuddin has five sons named Dabiruddin, Shams uddin, Mesbahuddin, Maisuddin and Miasuddin. Kalimuddin decided to live permanently in this country with his son Miasuddin as his 4 other sons were not willing to come. After the said Exchange Agreement Nagendra Nath Biswas and others registered a deed of Declaration and Irrevocable Power of attorney on 14-8-1965 duly authenticated by Notary Public appointing Mr. Miasuddin with their lawful Attorney for the purpose of effecting the exchange by registration of necessary documents in favour of Kalimuddin, Miasuddin came to this country and got physical possession of the exchanged property on behalf of his father who, thereafter made on oral gift of the exchanged property to Miasuddin on 15th December, 1965. Miasuddin submitted the Exchange Deed, on the strength of his power of Attorney, for validation before the A. D. C. (Rev), Khulna vide case No. 668/69-70 which. on transfer, has been recorded as case No. 668/69-70 of the office of A. D. C. (Rev.), Bagerhat and is pending there. Later on Kalimudding made a request of 5th of his Indian properties to his 4 sons including Miasuddin on 17-4-1979. Miasuddin being the owner in possession and enjoyment of the exchanged properties on the strength of registered kabalas dated 11-4-1984, 18-4-1984. 10-6-1984, 23-1-1984, 5-11-1986 sold the lands to the petitioners and the petitioners got the suit lands in their possession and they mutated their names in S. A. Khatians. They paid rents and got dakhilas. They also acquired title be adverse possession on the strength of physical, demarcated, continuous and open possession for more than 12 years. None of the sons of Kalimuddin except Miasuddin had ownership in the exchanged property. On the contrary, defendants created some documents using the name of the brother of Miasuddin and also held out threats on 3-4-1991 to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land which gave rise to the cause of action of the suit. 

 7. Mr. K. S. Zaman the learned  Advocate appearing for the petitioners has submitted that the learned Judge of the Court of appeal below reversed the order of injunction granted by the court of trial on the solitary ground that the land S. A. Khatian No. 378 is not clearly described in the schedule of the plaint and in the petition for temporary injunction and the learned Judge failed to observe that the land of Plot No. 200, 201 measuring 1.22 acres entitle constitute a single block of land and the plaintiffs clearly stated that they possess 60 acre out of the 2 plots from the eastern side even though they failed to mention by inadvertence of the learned Advocate as to what quantum of land of each plot is possessed by them. 

 8. Mr. Zaman has further submitted that the learned Judge should have found that it was no defect at all, but a mere irregular forensic parlance. And, while the learned Judge held that it was a defect, he should have been pleased to either direct the plaintiffs-petitioners to amend or grant injunction for the rest of the suit land excluding the said 2 plots to secure the ends of justice. Mr. Zaman has further submitted that the court of Appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice failing to observe that plot No. 200 and 201 measuring. 66 and 56 acres respectively of Khatian 378 constitute one block of land and it has been clearly stated in the schedule of the plaint and in the  petition for temporary injunction. Mr. Zaman  has further submitted that the learned court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by failing to direct the plaintiff petitioners to amend description of the suit land or, in the alternative, grant prayer for temporary injunction excluding Khatian No. 378 (of the said plots being plot Nos. 200. 201) to secure the ends of justice. Mr. Zaman further submitted that the learned Judge of the court below committed an error of law resulting in an the decision occasioning failure of his tice by misreading the pleadings of the petitioners and by not applying judicial mind to the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 16. In this cases Rule has been issued on 9-2-92 by the High Court Division (of the supreme Court of Bangladesh) while the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs petitioners has submitted that the amendment of the plaint has been done by the court of trial by order No. 30 dated 7-4-94 and I understand that the appellate Court correctly persuade the original plaint (Annexure-A of the revisional Application) and found that the 2 suit plots being plot Nos. 200, 201 of S. A. Khatian No. 378 were not fully described. Moreover I find that in S. A. Khatian No. 593 Plot No. 2328 and Plot. No. 2329 have Not been fully described and in such view of the matter I feel that the court of appeal below correctly persuade the original plaint  (before the amendment) and the court of appeal below committed no mistake in this regard. 

 18. In this case both the sides claim right, tittle and possession in the disputed land and the suit is still pending before the trial court. We are concerned here only with the for injunction. It is true that unless the suit plot, are clearly identified and specified the plaintiffs cannot get any order of injunction restraining the defendants to enter into the suit land. I find that the court of appeal below correctly analyzed from the plaint and the application for injunction of the plaintiffs that 2 suit plots being Nos. 200, 201 of S. A. Khatian No. 378 has not been correctly described. Moreover, I find from the original plaint filed along with revisional application (Annexure-A to the revisional application) that the lands of S. A. ichatian No. 593 Dag No. 2328 and 2329 have not been fully described. 

 19. Mr. Zaman while arguing for the plaintiff-petitioners submitted that ill description of the 2 suit plots in 200, 201 of S. A. Khatian No. 378 was mere irregularity and clerical mistake arising out of inadvertence of the learned lawyer for the defendant opposite parties vehemently argued that if the client cannot give full description of the suit plots how the lawyer can fill up the lacuna and as such some portions of the original plaint are remaining blank and vacant. I also think chat to get an order of injunction (being discretionary relief) from the court the plaintiffs are required to be vigilant and ill description of the plaint or the petition for injunction lay the plaintiffs deprives the plaintiffs from getting an order of injunction and agreeing with the decision of their Lordship Mr. Justice A. R. M. Aminul Islam Chowdhury and Mr. Justice Kazi Ebadul Huq as reported in 42 DLR (HCD) P-434 I find that the plaintiffs having failed to comply with the mandatory requirements of law in giving description sufficient to identify the suit land, they are not entitled to get any relief even if they succeed in proving their title and moreover the suit is still pending and whether the plaintiffs or defendants could get a decree in the suit requires to be decided by the trial court. I find no reason to interfere with the Judgment of the court of appeal below.
